title: Canary GPU workload federation and IaC promotion pipeline
author: Maya Singh
body:
Overview:

This runbook documents the end-to-end process for performing canary federations of GPU inference workloads across regions and for promoting the supporting Terraform/IaC modules and CI/CD artifacts. It ties together three areas that commonly surface flakiness during scale-ups: placement and affinity, egress capacity, and IaC promotion safety checks. Use this playbook for planned canaries and for emergency canary rollbacks when a rollout impacts latency, throughput, or tenant isolation.

Goals:
- Safely validate that a new runtime/driver/kernel release or a Terraform module change works for multi-region GPU workloads.
- Limit blast radius by starting with 1–5% production traffic and automated rollback triggers.
- Ensure IaC artifacts (terraform-module and promote jobs) can be promoted with automated checks and human approvals.

Applicability and scope:
- Applies to hosted inference clusters (redwood-infer-*) across us-west1, us-east4, eu-west1.
- Targets changes to: runtime kernel binary, gpu-node image, nvlink/networking config, and placement IaC modules (module/gpu-placement and module/egress-pool).
- Not for major schema changes to tenant billing or user data-plane migrations.

Pre-flight checks (automated and manual):
1) CI status: all gpu-ci/* and gpu-e2e/* pipelines green for at least 24h.
2) Terraform plan: module/gpu-placement and module/egress-pool plans reviewed; no destroy actions for shared resources.
3) Capacity check: Prometheus query (see Observability section) shows spare GPU slots >= 10% in target pools for expected canary load.
4) Egress credit escrow: egress-escrow ledger must show available credits >= projected canary egress (projected_token_count * avg_bytes_per_token / 1e9).
5) On-call notified: infra-sre and serving-runtime on-call paged; list in Ownership section.

Run steps (canary deploy):
1. Create a canary release tag: git tag canary/{short-commit} and push to origin.
2. Trigger CI pipeline: start gpu-ci/promote-canary job with BUILD_CANARY=true. This runs integration tests and builds the node image.
3. Terraform workspace: create a workspace canary-{region}-{date} and run terraform plan/apply for module/gpu-placement with var.canary_percent=1.
4. Configure routing: update the canary route (proxy/canary-route) to send initial 1% traffic. Use the routing CLI: redwoodctl route update --name canary-route --split 99:1 --target canary-v1.
5. Monitor baseline and canary metrics closely for 30 minutes. If stable, escalate to 5% after a 45 minute stabilization window.

Prometheus checks (automated):
- Latency p50/p95: (sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) - use dashboards/gpu-canary to compare baseline vs canary.
- Error rate: increase > 0.5% absolute or > 2x baseline over a rolling 5m triggers rollback.
- KV cache miss rate: > 10% relative increase signals warmup problem.
- Egress bandwidth: host_egress_bytes_rate > 80% of egress-pool allocation for 3m triggers canary throttle.

PromQL examples (copy into alerting rules or Grafana):
- Canary error rate: sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="canary-route",code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="canary-route"}[5m]))
- Baseline vs Canary p95 ratio: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"baseline|canary"}[5m])) by (le,route))

Terraform/IaC promotion gating (safety pipeline):
- Jobs involved: gpu-ci/terraform-plan, gpu-ci/terraform-apply-canary, gpu-ci/terraform-promote.
- Promotion gating criteria:
  * All integration tests passed in the canary workspace for 4 hours.
  * No severity-one alerts triggered against canary services for 2 hours.
  * Manual approval by two reviewers (infra lead + serving runtime owner).
- Sample minimal tf snippet for canary variable usage (module/gpu-placement):
```hcl
module "gpu_placement" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/module/gpu-placement.git//modules/placement"
  region = var.region
  canary_percent = var.canary_percent  # default 0, set to 1/5/10 for canary phases
}
```

Traffic ramp plan (recommended cadence):
1% -> 5% after 45m -> 20% after 2h -> 50% after 6h -> 100% after 24h (only if all checks pass).
At each step, wait the stabilization window and verify the automated checks.

Rollback criteria and steps (automated + manual):
Auto-rollback triggers:
- Error rate delta > 0.5% absolute within 10m window.
- p95 latency increase > 30% absolute or > 2x baseline.
- Egress pool saturates > 95% for > 3m.
Auto rollback action (CI/CD):
- gpu-ci/promote-canary job triggers redwoodctl route update --name canary-route --split 100:0 --target baseline-v1
Manual rollback steps:
1) If alerted, page serving-runtime and infra-sre.
2) Run: redwoodctl route update --name canary-route --split 100:0 --target baseline-v1
3) Terraform: revert canary workspace by setting var.canary_percent=0 and terraform apply.
4) Record incident in postmortem and tag related PRs.

Networking and locality specifics:
- Placement affinities: use placement-lane tags (affinity=nvlink, locality=zone-preferred) to keep multi-GPU jobs on nodes with NVLink. Avoid over-constraining; use preferred affinity rather than hard antiaffinity for canaries.
- Egress considerations: canary workloads may route to third-party services (metrics, evals). Use egress-escrow pools with separate Terraform-managed NAT gateways per region.

Operational checklist (pre-canary):
- [ ] CI green for 24h
- [ ] Terraform plan reviewed and no destructive shared changes
- [ ] egress-escrow >= projected consumption
- [ ] Spare GPU capacity >= 10% in target pools
- [ ] On-call paged and aware

Runbook escalation chain and contacts:
- Primary on-call: infra-sre (pager duty: infra-sre@redwood.com)
- Serving runtime on-call: serving-runtime@redwood.com
- Escalation: Eng Director oncall -> Platform PM -> Security if data exposure suspected

Ownership and responsibilities:
- infra-sre: workspace creation, terraform apply/rollback, egress-pool adjustments
- serving-runtime: node image validation, kernel rollouts, monitoring queries
- infra-platform: gating CI jobs, terraform module reviews

Post-canary activities (required before promote to production):
1) Run a short smoke test suite covering 10 tenants across regions (gpu-e2e/smoke).
2) Capture key traces for 24h and run the regression monitor against saved prompts.
3) Update the module CHANGELOG and add release notes to release-notes/gpu-canary/{tag}.
4) If promote criteria met, run gpu-ci/terraform-promote with manual approvals.

Useful commands and snippets:
- Start a canary apply: terraform workspace new canary-us-west1-20260210 && terraform apply -var="canary_percent=1"
- Update route: redwoodctl route update --name canary-route --split 99:1 --target canary-v1
- Force rollback: redwoodctl route update --name canary-route --split 100:0 --target baseline-v1

Example alert rule (sre-alerts.yaml snippet):
```yaml
- alert: CanaryErrorRateSpike
  expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="canary-route",code=~"5.."}[5m])) / sum(rate(http_requests_total{route="canary-route"}[5m])) > 0.005
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: Canary route error rate > 0.5%
```

Related pages and cross-references:
- module/gpu-placement (IaC)
- module/egress-pool (IaC)
- dashboards/gpu-canary
- runbooks/kv-cache-reconstruction-and-eviction-resilience-runbook.json

Change log and approvals:
- 2025-09-12: Initial draft by Maya Singh
- 2025-11-03: Added egress-escrow checks and Terraform gating - reviewer Daniel Kim
- 2026-02-10: Finalized automated rollback criteria and PromQL examples - reviewers Rosa Alvarez, Omar Haddad

Notes and rationale:
- Use small ramp steps and prefer preferred-affinity to avoid failing canaries because of strict placement constraints.
- Egress credit leaks are a common hidden failure mode—always pre-check the escrow ledger.
